title: NSM — Attack map and path
description: Where attacks come from and how far they get: the honeypot's own attackers, everything that reaches the sensor, and the route one intrusion takes from first packet to dropped file.

options.content:
## Where attacks come from, and how far they get
Live from the SSH honeypot on its own VM in its own VPC. The map places every attacking address by country; the graph below traces one intrusion's whole route — **arrived from → which program → what it typed → what it left behind.**

*My own test traffic is excluded by the queries. A country tells you where packets entered, not who sent them: the second-largest operator here runs from four countries at once.*

panels.title: Where the attacks come from
panels.description: Every address that reached the SSH honeypot, placed by the country its geolocation record claims. Circle size is sessions. Country here means what the database says, not where the operator sits — the same operator appears from several countries at once.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT src_country_code AS country_code, any(src_country) AS country,
       uniqExact(session) AS sessions, uniqExact(src_ip) AS addresses, count() AS events
FROM nsm.cowrie_events
WHERE src_ip NOT IN (SELECT address FROM nsm.lab_addresses) AND $__timeFilter(timestamp) AND src_country_code != ''
GROUP BY country_code ORDER BY sessions DESC

panels.title: Top origins
panels.description: The same data as the map, in the form that admits how little it means: one operator here spans four countries.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT src_country_code AS code, any(src_country) AS country, uniqExact(src_ip) AS addresses,
       uniqExact(session) AS sessions
FROM nsm.cowrie_events WHERE src_ip NOT IN (SELECT address FROM nsm.lab_addresses) AND $__timeFilter(timestamp) AND src_country_code != ''
GROUP BY code ORDER BY sessions DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: The path an attack takes
panels.description: One row per program, identified by its SSH client fingerprint: where its sessions arrived from, what it typed after logging in, and what it left behind. One program commonly spans several countries — which is why the country column above describes packet entry points rather than actors.

targets.rawSql:
WITH sess AS (
  SELECT session, anyIf(hassh, hassh != '') AS hassh, any(src_country_code) AS cc
  FROM nsm.cowrie_events
  WHERE src_ip NOT IN (SELECT address FROM nsm.lab_addresses) AND $__timeFilter(timestamp)
    AND src_country_code != ''
  GROUP BY session HAVING hassh != ''),
     ops AS (SELECT hassh, count() AS n FROM sess GROUP BY hassh ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 8)
SELECT substring(s.hassh, 1, 8)                                   AS program,
       arrayStringConcat(arraySort(groupUniqArray(s.cc)), ' ')    AS arrives_from,
       uniqExact(s.session)                                       AS sessions,
       uniqExact(e.src_ip)                                        AS addresses,
       substring(anyIf(e.input, e.eventid = 'cowrie.command.input' AND e.input != ''), 1, 46) AS typed,
       arrayStringConcat(arrayDistinct(groupArrayIf(
           extract(e.message, 'file "([^"]+)"'),
           e.eventid LIKE 'cowrie.session.file%' AND e.shasum != '')), ', ')                  AS left_behind
FROM nsm.cowrie_events AS e
INNER JOIN sess AS s ON e.session = s.session
WHERE s.hassh IN (SELECT hassh FROM ops)
GROUP BY program ORDER BY sessions DESC

panels.title: Everything that reaches the sensor
panels.description: Not just the honeypot: every connection Zeek logs where the far end is outside this lab, plus every Suricata alert source. Zeek decides which end is remote from its own local_nets, so the lab's own addresses cannot appear here.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT remote_country_code AS country_code, any(remote_country) AS country,
       uniqExact(remote_ip) AS addresses, count() AS connections
FROM nsm.zeek_conn
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND remote_country_code != '' AND direction = 'inbound'
GROUP BY country_code ORDER BY connections DESC

panels.title: Alerting networks
panels.description: Suricata alert sources by operator. Private sources (docker networks, the metadata server) return nothing from the geolocation database and are left blank rather than guessed at.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT src_country_code AS cc, substring(any(src_as_org), 1, 30) AS network,
       uniqExact(src_ip) AS addresses, count() AS alerts
FROM nsm.suricata_alert
WHERE $__timeFilter(timestamp) AND src_country_code != ''
GROUP BY cc, src_asn ORDER BY alerts DESC LIMIT 20
SELECT uniqExactIf(src_country_code, src_country_code != '') AS v FROM nsm.cowrie_events WHERE src_ip NOT IN (SELECT address FROM nsm.lab_addresses) AND $__timeFilter(timestamp)
SELECT uniqExact(src_ip) AS v FROM nsm.cowrie_events WHERE src_ip NOT IN (SELECT address FROM nsm.lab_addresses) AND $__timeFilter(timestamp)
SELECT uniqExact(session) AS v FROM nsm.cowrie_events WHERE src_ip NOT IN (SELECT address FROM nsm.lab_addresses) AND $__timeFilter(timestamp)

panels.title: Programs behind them
panels.description: Distinct SSH client fingerprints — far fewer than the addresses.

targets.rawSql: SELECT uniqExactIf(hassh, hassh != '') AS v FROM nsm.cowrie_events WHERE src_ip NOT IN (SELECT address FROM nsm.lab_addresses) AND $__timeFilter(timestamp)
